newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says feels better now than after surgery.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says feels better now than after surgery.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, walking stiffly but smiling and with colour in his cheeks, said on Wednesday he felt well compared to how he felt immediately after surgery.

In the first television pictures shown of him since his heart bypass operation on November 5, Yeltsin was shown walking in the grounds of Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital with members of his family.
Asked how he felt, the 65-year-old Kremlin leader replied: "Compared to the first days after the operation, fine."
Yeltsin, clad in a fur hat, checked woollen scarf and a long black coat, walked along a pathway of the hospital grounds with his wife, one of his two daughters and his granddaughter.
He said doctors had removed the surgery stitches on Wednesday and he expected to return to work after a spell at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow.

Doctors have said Yeltsin is recovering well from the seven-hour operation during which doctors replaced five blocked or damaged arteries with new blood vessels to improve the blood supply to his heart.
